items.followUp: Define acceleration and write its mathematical formula.

rubric.why: Rest is defined relative to the body's surroundings or a reference point.
rubric.description: Defines rest relative to surroundings/reference point.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the body's position does not change relative to its surroundings or a reference point.

rubric.why: Motion is defined by a change in position relative to surroundings or a reference point.
rubric.description: Defines motion as a change in position relative to surroundings/reference point.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the body's position changes relative to its surroundings or a reference point.

modelAnswer: A body is at rest if its position does not change relative to its surroundings.
A body is in motion if its position changes relative to its surroundings.

items.followUp: Define speed and write its mathematical formula.

rubric.why: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time.
rubric.description: Defines velocity as displacement per unit time.
rubric.how: Award for the definition using displacement and time.

rubric.why: The formula expresses velocity as displacement divided by time.
rubric.description: Gives the mathematical formula for velocity.
rubric.how: Award for a correct formula, including equivalent symbols.

modelAnswer: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time.

items.followUp: Why does a passenger jerk forward when a moving bus suddenly stops?

rubric.why: The passenger's body tends to preserve its state of motion due to inertia.
rubric.how: Award for naming inertia or inertia of motion.

rubric.why: As the bus changes direction, the passenger's body tends to continue along its original straight path, making the passenger move outward relative to the bus.
rubric.description: Explains the outward movement in terms of the body's tendency to continue in its original direction.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the body tends to continue in a straight line/original direction when the bus turns.

modelAnswer: When a bus takes a turn, its direction changes but the passenger's body tends to continue in its original straight-line direction due to inertia of motion.
Therefore, the passenger appears to move outward relative to the bus.

items.followUp: What is meant by an ideal rigid body?

rubric.why: The defining property is that distances between its particles remain unchanged.
rubric.description: States that distances between the body's particles remain constant.

rubric.why: A rigid body retains its shape and size.
rubric.description: States that the body's shape and size do not change.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it does not deform or its shape and size remain unchanged.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is an ideal body in which the distance between any two particles remains constant.
Thus, its shape and size do not change when forces act on it.

items.followUp: Give an example of a body in equilibrium at rest.

rubric.why: A body moving with constant velocity has zero acceleration and can be in equilibrium.
rubric.description: Gives a moving body with constant velocity.
rubric.how: Award for a valid example of uniform motion.

rubric.why: A body in equilibrium has zero resultant force; this makes the example physically valid.
rubric.description: Shows that the example is in equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award for stating that its forces are balanced or its net/resultant force is zero.

modelAnswer: A car moving in a straight line with constant velocity is an example of a moving body in equilibrium.
Its acceleration and resultant force are zero.

items.followUp: Define work and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Energy is defined as the capacity to do work.
rubric.description: Defines energy as the capacity or ability to do work.
rubric.how: Award for the standard definition of energy.

rubric.why: Kinetic and potential energy are the two types of mechanical energy.
rubric.description: Names the two types of mechanical energy.
rubric.how: Award for naming both kinetic energy and potential energy.

modelAnswer: Energy is the capacity to do work.
The two types of mechanical energy are kinetic energy and potential energy.

items.followUp: Write the formula for the efficiency of a system.

rubric.why: Efficiency compares the useful output with the input.
rubric.description: Identifies useful output relative to input as the basis of efficiency.
rubric.how: Award for stating that efficiency compares useful output to input.

rubric.why: Efficiency is the useful output divided by the input; it is multiplied by 100 when expressed as a percentage.
rubric.description: Gives the efficiency relationship or formula.
rubric.how: Award for the correct ratio, with × 100 when expressed as a percentage.

modelAnswer: The efficiency of a system is the ratio of its useful output to its input.

items.followUp: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease as we go higher above Earth's surface?

rubric.why: The amount of air above a location decreases with increasing height.
rubric.description: Links increasing height to a smaller column/amount of air above.
rubric.how: Award for noting that there is less air above at greater height.

rubric.why: The reduced weight of the air above exerts less pressure.
rubric.description: Explains that the reduced weight of air above causes lower pressure.
rubric.how: Award for connecting less air/less air weight above to decreased atmospheric pressure.

modelAnswer: As height above Earth's surface increases, the column of air above a location becomes smaller.
Its weight decreases, so it exerts less pressure; therefore, atmospheric pressure decreases with height.
